persona.name: Akiko Nishitani

occupation.title: Independent ERP Implementation Consultant
occupation.organization: Sole proprietor (kojin jigyonushi) serving manufacturing SMEs across Kansai
occupation.description: Left a major consulting firm at 34 to go independent. Juggles three client projects at a time, spending her days in requirement workshops and steering committees — about 10 meetings a week, half on-site in factories around Osaka and Hyogo. Every yen of software she buys comes out of her own pocket, so tools must earn their subscription monthly.

persona.education: Economics degree from Kobe University; SAP certification and a bookkeeping license (boki 2-kyu) acquired during her firm years.
long_term_goals: Stabilize at four retainer clients so she can stop chasing spot work
Publish a practical guide to SME system implementation
Buy a small condo instead of renting
Take every August fully off, non-negotiable
persona.style: Crisp and structured — she summarizes other people's rambling into three bullet points in real time, a habit clients pay for. Direct by Kansai standards but softens edges with self-deprecating humor. Hates wasting words; her emails are short enough that new clients sometimes mistake brevity for coldness.

traits: Self-reliant to the point of under-delegating

interests: Meeting documentation as a billable deliverable
AI tools that cut non-billable admin hours
likes: Tools that export clean Word/Excel deliverables
Clients who read what she sends
dislikes: Per-seat pricing designed for teams of fifty
Tools requiring an IT admin she doesn't have
Meetings that should have been emails

beliefs: Her minutes ARE the product — accuracy is her brand
A tool that saves an hour a week of unbilled work is cheap at 3,000 yen
Independence means every process must run without a back office
skills: Reading a client's real decision-maker within one meeting

general: Records client workshops (with permission) and reworks notes into formal minutes the same evening
Reviews her subscription list quarterly and cancels anything underused
Blocks Friday afternoons for admin and invoicing
Tests tools on one project before rolling into her standard kit

morning: 6:45 wake, stretching, tea instead of coffee
Reviews the day's meeting objectives on the train to client sites
workday: On-site workshops or video steering meetings
Evening: minutes, action item follow-ups, invoicing
evening: Done by 21:00 unless a deliverable is due
Wine study or a drama episode, lights out by 23:30
weekend: One onsen weekend a month when projects allow

health.physical: Good; recurring neck stiffness from laptop work on trains.
health.mental: Resilient, with periodic income-anxiety spirals between contracts that she manages by over-preparing proposals.

relationships.name: Fumie Nishitani
relationships.description: Lives in Wakayama; calls every Sunday and still asks when Akiko will 'get a proper company job' — it's a running joke now.

relationships.name: Taniguchi-san
relationships.description: Her best referral source; they trade industry gossip over yakitori quarterly.
